newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 7.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Monday:
- Northern Ireland faces a tense week as further parades planned between now and July 12 raise the political stakes and increase the potential for further sectarian violence.
- Violence intensified in many parts of the North this morning with widespread rioting and para-military attacks in the aftermath of the Garavaghy Road march.
- A total of 75 percent of Irish business leaders expect their company's turnover to increase in the next 12 months.
- Ireland is likely to retain its key Objective One status for EU funding -- but only for five years --in proposals for the 1999-2004 budget.
- Kilmeaden Advisory Committee, one of four advisory groups in Waterford, has again come out strongly against a proposed 337 million punt merger between Waterford and Avonmore.
- Slender hopes of an early IRA ceasefire were further dented last night as a wave of violence swept across nationalist areas of Northern Ireland.
- Health minister Brian Cowen was under increasing pressure last night to establish a public inquiry into drug trials carried out on orphanage children.
- The government will be forced to revalue the Irish pound by five or six percent within the next five or six weeks, according to a leading economist.
- A smoke alarm saved the lives of 16 people when fire destroyed a Donegal bungalow early yesterday morning.

- Violence erupted in nationalist areas of Northern Ireland last night as IRA gunmen opened fire on the security forces and vowed to avenge the British government's decision to allow yesterday's controversial Drumcree Orange parade.
- The Irish government is furious with Tony Blair and Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam over the decision to let the Drumcree march go ahead.
- Over 200,000 people are in for a cash and shares bonanza as First National Building Society finalises plans to go public.
